method.title: How it's calculated
method.pattern: A pattern is something that has happened in at least 80% of a team's previous matches in this same league: with 5 matches if it happened in all of them, and with 8 if not. This match and later ones never count.
method.contexts: It looks at this match's venue and at all venues, this season and over their last 10 matches at that venue or 20 overall, which may include the previous season.
method.lines: For each statistic, only the most demanding line that holds is shown. Anything that already happens in 80% of matches across the whole league is left out.
method.rival: The check looks at the complementary stat for the opponent, at their venue and over the same type of period: if one team scores away, whether the other concedes at home. Backed: the opponent meets it too, with a large enough sample. Partial: it meets it in at least half of their matches. Not backed: in fewer.
method.strength: Strength: both teams' matches are combined and we take the lower bound of the 95% Wilson interval, which penalises small samples (5 of 5 gives 0.57; 20 of 20, 0.84). High: the opponent backs it and the bound is at least 0.75. Medium: at least 0.60 and the opponent doesn't contradict it. Low: everything else.

history.note: Accumulators from 25/26 and 26/27 generated with a model trained only on earlier seasons, with rules fixed before seeing these matches, plus the matchdays played since then. They all count, including the ones that lost. <bold>Compare the hit rate with the promised probability</bold>: if they're similar, the model is reliable. ROI uses the odds shown, which for almost every accumulator are estimated with a bookmaker margin, so treat it as a rough guide.
